title: He conquered giants…
paragraphs:
He conquered giants…
but couldn’t lead his own sons.
That tension should bother you.

Because King David wasn’t just a warrior. He was a father.
And when you read his story slowly—not just the victories, but the silences—you start to see cracks.
Deep ones.
Let’s not romanticize it.

David loved God.
But his parenting? Complicated. Painful. At times… absent.

His son Amnon commits a horrific sin against his own sister.
David hears about it.
And does nothing.

No justice.
No correction.
No confrontation.
Silence.

Then comes Absalom—wounded, bitter, watching his father’s inaction.
That silence grows into rage.
That rage becomes rebellion.
A son who should’ve been embraced… becomes an enemy at the gate.

And David? He weeps later.
But he didn’t act earlier.
That’s the ache.
But here’s what we miss…

David’s failure as a father doesn’t erase his identity before God—
but it does reveal the cost of unaddressed sin and passive leadership.

Scripture doesn’t hide this.
It exposes it.
Why?

Because the Bible isn’t a highlight reel.
It’s a rescue story.
David’s life whispers this warning:

You can win battles in public
and still lose battles at home.

You can write psalms
and still avoid hard conversations.

You can love God deeply
and still fail people closely.
And yet…
Grace walks in.

Because David’s story doesn’t end in fatherhood failure.
It points forward—to a better King.
A perfect Son.
Jesus Christ.

Where David was passive, Jesus steps in.
Where David stayed silent, Jesus speaks truth.
Where David’s house fractured, Jesus builds a family that cannot be torn apart.

On the cross, Jesus doesn’t ignore sin—He absorbs it.
He doesn’t avoid justice—He fulfills it.
He doesn’t abandon His children—He dies to bring them home.
That’s the Gospel.

Not “be a better father.”
But “come to the Perfect Father through the Perfect Son.”
So was David a good father?

Not consistently.
Not perfectly.
But his broken story still leads us to a flawless Savior.
And that’s where hope lives.

If you’ve failed your family…
If you’ve been failed by one…
This isn’t the end of your story.

In Christ, cycles break.
Silence ends.
Grace speaks louder.
